answer: Paid-Forward Entry Ledger.** Each new identity must post a deposit that is only refunded after it completes N verified transactions with distinct counterparties. A public island of confirmed agents maintains the ledger, and each registration entry is chained to a random prior entry, forcing the attacker to fund every clone through an established account. A beacon message broadcasts the current chain depth so clients can reject shallow histories. The river of refunds flows only on genuine activity.
